h1: The 13 Best Monitor Privacy Screens Under $150 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Privacy Screens Under $150: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 13 monitor privacy filters scored on viewing angle, fit data and finish, from 24-inch pairs to a 15.6-inch laptop screen.
summary: The Vxaop 27 inch pair is the best overall, the only listing to publish a 60 degree viewing cone alongside a matte coating. The Peslv 27 inch pair adds a reversible surface, the Protescreen is a plain 27 inch pair, and the Mamol prints exact dimensions. At 24 inches, Magicmoon, Syhauifei and Peslv cover most needs, with PYS the only laptop filter.
intro: Every filter in this group costs well under $150, so budget is not the question. The real question is whether a listing lets you check fit and performance before you pay. A filter cut a few millimetres small leaves a bright border around the screen, and one with no stated viewing angle is a guess about how well it hides your work from the person next to you.

Our editors ranked thirteen filters on what their specification sheets state: exact dimensions, viewing cone, finish and pack size. Self-reported light-blocking figures are noted as the maker's own claims. A filter that publishes its numbers beats one that only says dark from the side, because only the former can be checked against your monitor.

products.name: Vxaop 2-Pack 27 Inch Privacy Screen Filter
products.verdict: The one listing here that publishes its viewing angle, glare coating and blue light claim.
products.description:
The Vxaop pair has the most specific spec sheet of the thirteen. It states a 60 degree viewing cone, an anti-glare matte coating and a blue light reduction claim, and it ships as two filters for 27 inch 16:9 monitors in the $25 to $50 bucket. A published viewing angle tells you how far off-centre a neighbour must sit to read the screen.

It ranks first because you can verify what you are buying before you click. A narrower cone hides more, but it also narrows your own comfortable seating.

Buy it for open-office work on a 27 inch panel. The caveats: matte softens fine detail, so photo and video editors should skip it, and the blue light figure is the maker's own claim, not an independent measurement.
cons: Blue light claim is the maker's own
products.skipIf: You edit photos or video and need perfect colour.

products.name: Peslv 2-Pack 27 Inch Privacy Screen
products.verdict: A reversible 27-inch pair with a stated 92 percent light-filtering figure.
products.description:
The Peslv 27 inch pair uses a double-sided surface, so one face is glossy and the other matte. The listing says the optical film is imported from Japan and claims a 92 percent light-filtering figure at side angles, and the pair is sized for 27 inch 16:9 panels.

It sits just under the Vxaop because it gives no viewing angle in degrees, and the filtering number is self-reported. Reversibility is its edge, since you can flip the filter to suit your lighting.

Choose it if you sit near a window and want to try both finishes. Skip it if you need a published angle. The caveat: you still need to confirm that the cut matches your panel, so measure the visible area before you order.
products.idealFor: People near windows who want to try two finishes.
products.skipIf: You want a published viewing angle.

products.name: Protescreen 2-Pack 27 Inch Privacy Screen
products.verdict: A plain 27-inch pair from a seller that says it has revised the design 200 times.
products.description:
The Protescreen pair gives you two filters for 27 inch 16:9 monitors, in a simple cut-to-size design. The seller says the design has gone through 200 updates, which is a claim about iteration, not about how well the film performs.

It ranks below Peslv and Vxaop because the listing offers few measurable specs, so you are choosing on trust. Its strength is a straightforward two-piece pack in the $25 to $50 bucket.

Buy it to fit out two desks with the same panel size. Skip it if you want a stated viewing angle. The caveat is fit: with fewer numbers published, a few millimetres of error would leave a bright border, so measure the visible panel first and check the return policy.
cons: Fit depends on exact panel size
products.skipIf: You want a stated viewing angle.

products.name: Mamol 2-Pack 27 Inch Privacy Filter
products.verdict: Lists exact panel dimensions so you can match your monitor before ordering.
products.description:
Mamol prints the fit dimensions for its 27 inch filter: 598 by 337 mm. It markets the screen as blacking out content from the side and reducing eye strain, and it ships as a pair.

That dimension line is why it outranks several thinner listings. You can lay a tape across your panel and confirm a match before ordering, which removes the most common failure with film filters. It trails Peslv because there is no reversible finish and no stated filtering percentage.

Buy it if you are fit-conscious and own a standard 16:9 panel. The caveat: it publishes no viewing angle, so you do not know how narrow the cone is. Skip it if your monitor is ultrawide or 16:10, because the cut will not suit.
products.skipIf: Your monitor is not a standard 16:9.

products.name: Magicmoon 2-Pack 24 Inch Privacy Filter
products.verdict: A 24-inch pair aimed squarely at shared and open work spaces.
products.description:
Magicmoon sells two 24 inch filters for 16:9 monitors, measured diagonally. The listing says the screen appears dark from the side and pitches the pair for open work spaces, where colleagues walk behind desks.

It leads the 24 inch group on clarity of purpose, but it publishes fewer numbers than Syhauifei or Peslv. It fits 24 inch panels only, so a 23.8 or 25 inch monitor may not match.

Buy it for an open office with a standard 24 inch screen. The caveat: with few measurable specs listed, you cannot confirm the viewing cone or the exact cut dimensions. Ask the seller for the width and height in millimetres, and compare with your visible panel before ordering.
products.skipIf: Your panel is not exactly 24 inches.

products.name: Syhauifei 2-Pack 24 Inch Privacy Screen
products.verdict: Micro-louver film with full 24-inch dimensions and mounting included.
products.description:
Syhauifei uses what it calls an upgraded micro-louver film and lists its 24 inch fit as 609.6 mm diagonal, 532 mm wide and 299 mm tall. Two simple mounting options come with the pair. Micro-louver means tiny vertical slats that block side light.

Printed dimensions put it ahead of Magicmoon for fit confidence. It ranks below the 24 inch Peslv because that listing adds a reversible surface and a light-filtering figure.

Choose it if you want to confirm fit before you pay. The caveats are that it gives no filtering figure, and micro-louver film slightly darkens the screen, so expect to raise brightness a little. Skip it if you want a reversible finish.
products.idealFor: 24-inch users who want to confirm fit first.

products.name: Peslv 2-Pack 24 Inch Privacy Screen
products.verdict: The 24-inch twin of the Peslv 27, with a reversible face.
products.description:
Peslv's 24 inch pair repeats the 27 inch formula: a double-sided surface, optical film said to be imported from Japan and a 92 percent light-filtering claim. The reversible face lets you choose glossy or matte.

It carries the strongest 24 inch spec sheet, yet it lands lower than the 27 inch version because it costs noticeably more than the 24 inch rivals. Compared with the Mamol 24 inch, the reversible surface is the reason to pay extra.

Buy it for a 24 inch screen near a window, where reflections are a daily nuisance. The caveats: no viewing angle in degrees, and the claims are self-reported rather than independently measured. If you only need a clean fit, Syhauifei is cheaper.

products.name: Mamol 2-Pack 24 Inch Privacy Filter
products.verdict: A simple 24-inch pair that prints its width as 532 mm.
products.description:
Mamol lists its 24 inch filter width as 532 mm, and says it blacks out content from the side and eases eye strain. It ships as a pair, and is the same product as the 27 inch Mamol in a smaller cut.

It matches Syhauifei on width but lacks mounting detail and a film description, which is why it ranks lower. The listing is brief, so there is little to weigh beyond fit and price.

Fine for a basic 24 inch fit without extras. Choose it if you want a pair at a low price and are comfortable with a plain filter. The caveats are the little film detail and no mounting information, so check that you have a way to hold the filter on the screen before you order.
products.skipIf: You want reversible or published angles.

products.name: SightPro 24 Inch Privacy Screen Filter
products.verdict: A single 24-inch multi-layer film filter, not a pair.
products.description:
SightPro sells one filter for a 24 inch 16:9 monitor, listed at 532 by 299 mm. It describes a multi-layered film that blacks out the screen from the side, and the dimensions are published, which helps fit.

It ranks lower than the two-packs because you get one filter, so a second desk costs a second purchase. It is, though, the simplest way to protect a single 24 inch monitor, with no leftover filter in a drawer.

Buy it for one monitor on a $25 to $50 budget. The caveat is cost per screen: a pair from Syhauifei or Magicmoon gives you two filters for similar money. Skip it if you have more than one monitor, because the arithmetic does not favour a single filter.

products.name: Hanging Removable 24 Inch Privacy Screen 2-Pack
products.verdict: A hanging design that skips adhesive and installs quickly.
products.description:
This pair hangs on the monitor instead of sticking on, so it is removable. The listing gives 547 by 320 mm and says that unlike adhesive filters it does not need an exact fit, which makes it forgiving of slightly different panel sizes.

It ranks mid-table because removability matters only if you share a screen, and it is the priciest 24 inch pair here. The larger frame, 547 by 320 mm, suits monitors with thicker bezels.

Choose it for a shared computer that needs the filter off for presentations or screen sharing. Skip it if you prefer a flush finish. The caveat: a hanging filter can slip on a thin bezel, and the larger frame looks bulkier than a film that sits flat on the screen.
products.idealFor: Shared screens that need the filter off at times.

products.name: PYS Magnetic Laptop Privacy Screen 15.6 Inch
products.verdict: The only laptop filter here, attaching magnetically and not for touchscreens.
products.description:
PYS makes a magnetic privacy filter for 15.6 inch 16:9 laptops. The listing stresses easy magnetic installation and glare reduction, and warns that it is not optimized for touchscreens. A magnetic attachment means you can remove it when you present.

It ranks near the bottom only because it targets a different device from the monitor filters. For laptops it is the one that matters in this guide.

Buy it for a non-touch 15.6 inch laptop that travels, such as on trains or in cafes. Skip it if your laptop has a touchscreen, because the filter says it is not optimized for one. The caveat is size: it comes in one size, so a 14 or 17 inch laptop needs a different filter.

products.name: Computer Privacy Screen Filter 24 Inch 16:9
products.verdict: A reversible single 24-inch filter, with visible area stated as 532 by 299 mm.
products.description:
This 24 inch filter lists a visible display area of 532 by 299 mm and is reversible, letting you choose glossy or matte. The listing notes it does not block visibility directly behind you, which is true of every filter of this type.

It sits near the bottom because the detail is thin, but reversibility is rare at this price. Compared with the two-pack options, you get one filter and fewer specs.

Reasonable for one 24 inch monitor if you want a choice of finish. Skip it if you need privacy from directly behind, since no film filter provides that. The caveats are sparse performance specs and the single-filter pack, so a second monitor means a second purchase.
cons: Does not block view from behind
products.idealFor: One 24-inch monitor with a choice of finish.
products.skipIf: You need privacy from directly behind.

products.name: Computer Privacy Screen Filter 27 Inch 16:9
products.verdict: The 27-inch sibling, 598 by 337 mm and reversible.
products.description:
The 27 inch version lists a visible area of 598 by 337 mm and the same reversible finish as the 24 inch. It ships as a single filter, with the same note that it does not block a view from behind.

It ranks last because the listing is thin and offers one filter. Against the Vxaop pair it gives up numbers and quantity, and the viewing cone is not stated.

Only worth it as a single-screen budget option, for someone who wants a reversible face on one 27 inch monitor. The caveat: with limited performance data, you are taking the maker's word for the filtering. The Mamol 27 inch publishes the same fit dimensions as a pair.
products.idealFor: One 27-inch monitor on a tight budget.
products.skipIf: You want a pair or published angles.

methodology.title: Published viewing angle
methodology.description: Filters that state a viewing cone in degrees scored above those that only say the screen looks dark from the side.

methodology.title: Fit data
methodology.description: We rewarded listings that print exact width and height, since a wrong cut leaves a visible gap.

methodology.title: Finish choice
methodology.description: Reversible glossy and matte surfaces earned credit because glare varies by room.

methodology.title: Pack value
methodology.description: Two filters per pack beat a single filter at similar size, judged against the other listings in this guide.

methodology.title: Install method
methodology.description: Magnetic, hanging and film mounting each suit different use, so we ranked each against its own purpose.

whatMatters.factor: Measure the visible area, not the diagonal
whatMatters.detail: Filters are cut to a specific width and height, so two 24 inch monitors can differ by several millimetres. Measure the visible panel without the bezel, then compare with the listing, such as 532 by 299 mm for a common 24 inch 16:9. A filter cut small leaves a bright edge, and one cut large will not sit flat, so a few millimetres matter.

The viewing cone sets how far from centre a neighbour can still read your screen. A narrower cone, like the 60 degrees on the Vxaop listing, hides more but also narrows your own comfortable seating. Look for a degree figure, not just the word dark, since an unstated cone cannot be compared across filters or checked against your seating.

Matte cuts window reflections but slightly softens text, while glossy keeps sharpness and shows glare. Reversible filters let you try both, which matters if you sit near a window or work with fine detail. Look for double-sided or reversible wording in the listing, and note that a matte finish suits spreadsheets more than photo work.

Every filter here fits 16:9 panels. An ultrawide or a 16:10 monitor will not fit, so check your panel ratio in its specs first. Touchscreens are another limit, as the PYS laptop filter says it is not optimized for them. Measure width and height rather than relying on the diagonal alone, and keep the receipt.

Adhesive-free hanging and magnetic filters come off for presentations, while film filters sit flush for a cleaner look. Decide whether you need to remove the filter often, then choose between the hanging pair and a flush option. A hanging design is also more forgiving about panel size, but it slips more easily.

faq.q: Do privacy screens work from directly behind me?
faq.a: No. A privacy filter narrows the side viewing angle only. The Computer Privacy Screen Filter listing itself notes it does not block visibility directly behind you, so a person standing behind your chair can still read the screen.

faq.q: Will a privacy filter make my screen dimmer?
faq.a: Yes, a little. The micro-louver film reduces light at every angle, so you may raise brightness slightly. A matte coating, as on the Vxaop, also softens fine text, which some users notice at once.

faq.q: How do I know which size to buy?
faq.a: Measure the visible panel width and height without the bezel and compare with the listed dimensions, for example 532 by 299 mm for many 24 inch 16:9 panels or 598 by 337 mm at 27 inches.

faq.q: Is the Peslv worth it over the Mamol?
faq.a: If you want to try glossy and matte, yes, because the Peslv has a reversible surface. If you only care about fit, the Mamol's printed dimensions are enough, which keeps the choice simple.

faq.q: Can I use these on a touchscreen?
faq.a: The PYS laptop filter says it is not optimized for touchscreens, and the same caution applies to film filters in general. Test on a non-touch panel first, and keep the return window in mind.
They can slip on thin bezels. The hanging pair is meant to avoid adhesive, so check your bezel thickness before ordering, and make sure the frame sits securely at the top of the monitor.

finalTake: Buy the Vxaop pair for a 27 inch 16:9 monitor, and the Mamol if fit certainty matters most. At 24 inches, Syhauifei prints the fullest dimensions and the Peslv adds a reversible face. Use PYS for a non-touch 15.6 inch laptop. Always measure the visible panel before ordering.
